description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of a reasoning-based large language model (LLM) across five distinct categories, labeled 0 through 4 on the horizontal axis, by comparing the proportions of “Incorrect” and “Correct” responses, as indicated by the legend: blue dotted bars represent “Incorrect” and magenta striped bars represent “Correct.” The vertical axis, labeled “γB,” ranges from 0.0 to approximately 0.7, with major gridlines at 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and minor tick marks at 0.1 intervals. For each category, the “Correct” bar is consistently taller than the “Incorrect” bar, indicating higher accuracy. Specifically, in category 0, “Incorrect” is approximately 0.41 and “Correct” is approximately 0.69; in category 1, “Incorrect” is about 0.40 and “Correct” is about 0.67; in category 2, “Incorrect” is around 0.36 and “Correct” is around 0.64; in category 3, “Incorrect” is approximately 0.33 and “Correct” is approximately 0.62; and in category 4, “Incorrect” is about 0.29 and “Correct” is about 0.46. The chart visually conveys a general trend of declining performance across categories, with both correct and incorrect proportions decreasing from left to right, though the correct rate remains substantially higher than the incorrect rate in all cases. The chart is part of a study titled “Mapping the Minds of LLMs: A Graph-Based Analysis of Reasoning LLM,” suggesting the categories may correspond to different reasoning tasks or graph-based cognitive steps.
